result.summary: Bumps the minimum supported Clang compiler version from 17 to 19, updates CI images/packages accordingly, switches the CTAD feature check to test alias-template CTAD instead of aggregate CTAD, sets clang-format to use the latest standard, and adds a release note. Targeted for the 33.0 release (2027).
result.problem: Old Clang minimums force the project to carry workarounds for compiler bugs and prevent adoption of newer C++20 features (CTAD for alias templates); this mainly affects maintainers/contributors who want to simplify code, not end users.

result.card: This PR bumps Bitcoin Core's minimum supported Clang version from 17 to 19, updates CI images and dependency docs accordingly, and adjusts a CTAD feature check plus clang-format settings. It targets the 33.0 release, expected in 2027, and its main benefit is letting future code drop workarounds for old Clang bugs, per the author's description. The PR is a draft with failing CI and has received no reviewer engagement at all, so both reviewability and agreement are effectively unassessed. There is no urgency or deadline cited, making this a routine, deferrable maintenance bump rather than a pressing build issue.
